title: Datalähtöisen ja AI-avusteisen asiakasohjauksen kehittämiskumppanuus
description: Datalähtöisen ja AI-avusteisen asiakasohjauksen kehittämiskumppanuus HANKINNAN TAUSTA Strateginen suunta kohti vuotta 2030 Business Finlandin Strategia 2030:n keskeisenä tavoitteena on saavuttaa julkishallinnon paras asiakaskokemus sekä kasvattaa Business Finlandin vaikuttavuutta suomalaisen elinkeinoelämän uudistumisessa, kasvussa ja kansainvälistymisessä. Tavoitteen saavuttaminen edellyttää siirtymistä nykyisistä osittain manuaalisista, reaktiivisista ja asiantuntijariippuvaisista toimintamalleista kohti tietojohtoista, ennakoivaa ja skaalautuvaa asiakasohjausta. Digitalisaation tavoitteena ei ole yksinomaan järjestelmien kehittäminen tai teknologian käyttöönotto, vaan toimintatapojen, prosessien ja kyvykkyyksien kokonaisvaltainen uudistaminen. Business Finland haluaa hyödyntää dataa, analytiikkaa ja tekoälyä asiakkaidensa tunnistamisessa, ohjaamisessa ja palvelemisessa sekä vapauttaa asiantuntijoidensa aikaa tausta- tai rutiinitehtävistä vaikuttavampaan asiakastyöhön. Samanaikaisesti tavoitteena on vahvistaa asiakkaiden kuuntelemista ja asiakasymmärryksen hyödyntämistä osana palveluiden, toimintamallien ja asiakkuuksien kehittämistä. Asiakaskokemusta, asiakasohjauksen vaikuttavuutta sekä palveluiden käyttöä seurataan ja mitataan systemaattisesti, jotta toimintaa voidaan jatkuvasti kehittää tiedolla johdetusti. Transformaation onnistumista arvioidaan muun muassa seuraavilla mittareilla: • asiakaskokemus ja asiakkaiden suosittelu • asiakasohjauksen osuvuus • palveluihin ohjautuminen • palveluiden käyttöaste • asiakastarpeiden tunnistamisen onnistuminen • asiakasaktivoinnin vaikuttavuus • asiakkuuksien kehitys ja palveluiden hyödyntäminen • asiantuntijatyön tehokkuus ja automaation hyödyntäminen • datan, analytiikan ja tekoälyn hyödyntämisen aste • Business Finlandin strategisten tavoitteiden toteutumista tukevat vaikuttavuusmittarit. Nykytilan haasteet ja tarve muutokselle Business Finland on toteuttanut datalla johdetun asiakasohjauksen esiselvityksen, jonka yhteydessä on tunnistettu useita nykytilan kehityskohteita ja pullonkauloja. Näiden ratkaisemiseksi tarvitaan pitkäjänteinen kehittämiskumppani tukemaan organisaation muutosta. Keskeiset tunnistetut haasteet ovat: 1. Tiedon hajanaisuus ja rajallinen asiakasymmärrys: Asiakkaisiin, markkinoihin, palveluihin, asiointiin, vuorovaikutukseen ja verkostoihin liittyvä tieto on hajautunut useisiin järjestelmiin, tietovarantoihin ja ulkoisiin tietolähteisiin. Tämän vuoksi organisaatiolla ei ole yhtenäistä ja ajantasaista näkymää asiakkaisiin, asiakkaiden tarpeisiin, potentiaaliin, palveluiden käyttöön, asiointihistoriaan eikä asiakkuuden nykytilaan. Tämä vaikeuttaa asiakkaiden tunnistamista, kohdentamista, priorisointia sekä oikea-aikaista palveluohjausta. 2. Proaktiivisuuden puute ja AI-avusteisen asiakasohjauksen rajallinen hyödyntäminen: Business Finlandilta puuttuu systemaattinen kyvykkyys tunnistaa, priorisoida ja ohjata oikeat asiakkaat oikeisiin palveluihin oikeaan aikaan. AI-avusteisen analytiikan, kohdentamisen ja palveluohjauksen hyödyntäminen on vielä rajallista, mikä heikentää asiakasohjauksen vaikuttavuutta ja skaalautuvuutta. 3. Manuaalinen asiakasohjaus ja asiantuntijoiden tunnistaminen: Asiakkaiden tarpeiden yhdistäminen oikeisiin palveluihin, asiantuntijoihin, verkostoihin ja ekosysteemeihin perustuu nykyisin pitkälti manuaaliseen tiedonhakuun ja yksittäisten asiantuntijoiden kokemukseen. Organisaatiolta puuttuu AI-avusteinen kyvykkyys tunnistaa asiakkaan tilanteeseen parhaiten soveltuvat palvelut, asiantuntijat ja yhteistyömahdollisuudet sekä tukea asiantuntijoita oikea-aikaisilla suosituksilla. Tämä hidastaa palveluprosessia, vaikeuttaa tiedon hyödyntämistä ja heikentää asiakasohjauksen skaalautuvuutta. Tavoitetila: Datalla johdetun ja AI-avusteisen asiakasohjauksen malli Pitkän aikavälin visiona on rakentaa yhtenäiseen asiakaskuvaan, datalähtöiseen päätöksentekoon, tekoälyavusteiseen asiakasohjaukseen sekä moderniin data- ja AI-kyvykkyyteen perustuva toimintamalli. Tavoitteena on muodostaa kokonaisvaltainen näkymä asiakkaisiin, heidän tarpeisiinsa, potentiaaliinsa, asiointiinsa ja palveluiden käyttöön sekä hyödyntää tätä tietoa asiakkaiden tunnistamisessa, ohjaamisessa ja kehittämisessä. Tavoitetilassa asiakkaan polku jakautuu kolmeen vaiheeseen, joiden digitaalista kyvykkyyttä Toimittajan tulee tukea kehittämään: 1. Tunnista & tavoita Hyödynnämme sisäisiä ja ulkoisia tietolähteitä tunnistaaksemme uusia potentiaalisia kasvuyrityksiä sekä ennakoidaksemme asiakkaiden tarpeita. Asiakkaille kohdennetaan oikea-aikaisesti heidän tilanteeseensa sopivia palveluita, sisältöjä, tapahtumia ja yhteydenottoja datan, analytiikan ja AI-avusteisen kohdentamisen avulla. 2. Palvele & ratkaise Autamme asiakkaita löytämään heidän tilanteeseensa parhaiten soveltuvat palvelut, rahoitusinstrumentit, asiantuntijat, verkostot ja kansainvälistymismahdollisuudet. AI-avusteinen asiakasohjaus tukee tarpeiden tunnistamista, asiantuntijoiden työtä, palveluiden suosittelua sekä asiakkaiden ohjautumista tarkoituksenmukaisiin palvelupolkuihin. 3. Seuraa & syvennä Hyödynnämme tietoa asiakkaiden kehityksestä, palveluiden käytöstä ja asiointihistoriasta asiakkuuksien jatkuvaan kehittämiseen. Ennakoimme asiakkaiden tulevia tarpeita ja suosittelemme proaktiivisesti seuraavia palveluita, verkostoja, ohjelmia ja kehittämispolkuja asiakkaan kasvun, kansainvälistymisen ja vaikuttavuuden tukemiseksi. Tämän vuoksi Business Finland etsii kumppania, joka ei ainoastaan toimita teknistä koodia tai arkkitehtuurikuvauksia, vaan kykenee viemään muutoksen läpi kaikilla tasoilla: luomassa arvoa tuottavia käyttötapauksia, rakentamassa vankkaa kyvykkyysperustaa, uudistamassa organisaation yhteistä kieltä ja operointimallia sekä johtamassa kulttuurista muutosta ja asiantuntijoiden datalukutaitoa.,

title: Educational Services
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. As per the Commissioner’s Directive 720 (Education Programs and Services for Offenders), when an inmate's grade level is below grade 12 or its provincial equivalent, education will be identified as a need in their Correctional Plan. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to: a. Facilitate inmates' reintegration by increasing educational skill levels through the provision of accredited programs. b. Ensure education programs and library services respect gender, ethnic, cultural and linguistic differences, and are responsive to the special needs of women inmates, Indigenous inmates, inmates requiring mental health care and other groups. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: To provide educational services to the inmates at Nova Institution for Women. 1.2 Tasks: 1 The Contractor must provide the following resources: a. Two (2) teachers/instructors who must provide teaching services - 35 hours per week at 7 hours per day - Monday to Friday 2 The Contractor must deliver the following educational services: a. Adult Basic Education program (ABE); b. Adapted ABE programs for offenders with learning difficulties and disabilities; c. Educational programs leading to the Adult High School Diploma; d. Other education programs, pilot programs, digital education and any other curriculum the Project Authority requests; e. Coordination of post-secondary pre-requisite courses, correspondence courses and other programs including but not limited to, the Walls to Bridges program; f. Provide appropriate provincially recognized certificates, following course and level completions. 3. One (1) of the certified teachers must be designated as Lead teacher to: a. Ensure bilingual educational services at the school, in the Secure Unit (SU) and in the Structured Intervention Unit (SIU); b. Establish and coordinate schedules for the teachers/instructors; c. Ensure teachers/instructors follow the prescribed provincial curriculum; d. Ensure teachers/instructors provide quality educational services to offenders; e. Maintain enrolments in education programs at full capacity; f. Teach and facilitate independent studies (cell studies); g. Review all incoming inmates’ education information and provide parole officers with data necessary to make referrals to education programs; h. Evaluate the inmates’ educational needs, waitlists and suspensions; i. Administer and score the Canadian Adult Achievement Test and the “Test de rendement pour francophones” or other assessment tools approved by the Project Authority; j. Offer educational counseling to students; k. Adjust and combine classes to ensure continuity of educational services to inmates, in the event of teacher/instructor absences; l. Perform other related tasks to ensure proper operation of the school; m. Submit requests to the Project Authority for the purchase of pedagogical resources and office/school supplies; n. Participate in the Correctional Interventions Board (CIB) meetings and provide information/recommendations; o. Follow the CIB guidelines in terms of assigning inmates based on the student-to-teacher ratio to maximize education program capacity; p. Collaborate with the CIB to assign inmates to the educational tutor positions. The Contractor must work in collaboration with CSC to hire inmate classroom tutors. This must include in classroom training and orientation of the tutor by the contract teacher/instructor; q. Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator to assign volunteer community tutors to the classrooms; r. Participate in meetings as requested by the Project Authority; s. Supervise contract teachers/instructors, monitor and coordinate visits relative to the education programs; t. Participate in the yearly development of the annual education program plan (AEPP); u. Assist the Project Authority with input, data analysis, and reporting, as it relates to the educational results, prior learning assessment and recognition (PLAR) credits, progress, forecasting, curriculum development, digital programs, pilot programs, and digital education; v. Ensure an efficient information-sharing process such as e-mails pertaining to work safety, security reminders, and general information which is deemed necessary to inform personnel and to maintain a safe and secure environment; w. Organize and invigilate Canadian Adult Education Credential (CAEC) testing sessions and other assessments in both official languages, which may take place during the evening or during institutional operational hours; x. Always ensure, that resources, services, and communication are available in both official languages; y. Ensure that all communication and information is sent to all institutional staff in both official languages and pre-approved by the Project Authority or the Program Manager. 4. Contract teachers/instructors must: a. Provide individualized teaching and education plans; b. Assess the academic needs and aptitudes of inmates; c. Ensure inventory control of CSC assets always related to education programs; d. Provide a variety of teaching strategies (including, but not limited to individualized learning, group learning, guests’ presentations); e. Employ classroom management techniques and methods to ensure the protection and preservation of educational resources (including, but not limited to books, supplies, equipment); f. Complete daily visual searches of the installations before and after each teaching sessions; g. Complete observation reports and immediately submit to CSC security personnel any information or observations of incidents that could jeopardize the safety or the security of others. This may include charging inmates for various infractions; h. Supervise and evaluate the inmate cleaner in the school area according to CD-730 “Offender Program Assignment and Inmate Payments”; i. Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator to guide and monitor the community volunteer tutors in the classroom; j. Prepare and take steps to recognize significant cultural dates and months by providing presentations, collages, and other forms of visual reminders to staff and inmates throughout the school; k. Cooperate and collaborate with CSC management, staff, and other contractors. 1.3 Expected results: Provision of education services to enable inmates to achieve grade 12 or its provincial equivalent. 1.4 Performance standards: 1. The Contractor must ensure that the contract teachers/instructors understand and adhere to the following CSC policies, guidelines and procedures: a. CD 001 - Mission, Values and Ethics Framework of the Correctional Service of Canada : https://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/acts-and-regulations/001-cd-en.shtml b. CSC Policy (Commissioner Directives and Standard Operating Practices) and Legislation: https://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/acts-and-regulations/005006-0001-en.shtml i. CD 350: Contracting and Material Management ii. CD 568-1: Recording and Reporting of Security Incidents iii. CD 577: Staff Protocol in Women Offender Institutions iv. CD 701: Information Sharing v. CD 720: Education Programs and Services for Offenders vi. CD 720-1: Guidelines for Education Programs vii. CD 730: Offender Program Assignments and Inmate Payments viii. CD 764: Access to Materials ix. Program Strategy for Federally Sentenced Women x. C

description: The objective of this purchase is to acquire a high-performance research-grade Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer capable of advanced infrared spectroscopic measurements across the mid-IR and far-IR regions, with high spectral resolution, vacuum optics, time-resolved measurement capability, multiple detector/source configurations, and flexible sample/accessory compatibility. title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) Solicitation #: 30008053 This requirement is for Fisheries and Oceans Canada Title: Stream to Sea Program Delivery and Coordination Services: South Coast – Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands Objective: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, requires Contractors to provide delivery and coordination services for the Stream to Sea Program, as defined by the Project Authority, for schools within School Districts listed below, as well as Independent Schools, other Learning Centres, and community partners in the same geographic area: Victoria, Sooke, Saanich and Southern Gulf Islands (including School Districts (SD) 61, 62, 63, 64) Stream to Sea Program delivery and coordination services are required over the entire duration of this Contract with some times requiring more commitment than others. Delivery and coordination services will be defined on a geographic specific basis through the development of work plan details using the information provided in Appendix 1 (Scope of Work). The Contractor will work with the Project Authority, to coordinate and deliver the Stream to Sea Program in schools and with local community groups. The work will consist of training educators, coordinating and assisting with set up of classroom incubators (aquaria), delivering salmon eggs to schools, providing classroom (indoor and outdoor) sessions which may include the salmon life cycle, fish dissections, aquatic ecosystems and habitat requirements for salmon, environmental sustainability as it relates to salmon, stream to sea migration and other salmon focused education pertinent to the area. The Contractor will provide trouble shooting and maintenance support for aquaria in schools and develop or assist with the development and delivery of a spring fry release program for participating schools. In some instances, the Contractor may participate in the live transport of adult and juvenile salmon and may participate in the spawning of broodstock. Contractor will also support Pacific Region tracking and reporting (i.e. brood stock summary and year end stream to sea data collection/reporting). The Stream to Sea Program aims to develop opportunities for external parties to be involved. Contractors may be required to facilitate and develop opportunities with local communities, First Nations, and community groups. Security Requirement: There is no security associated with this requirement. Period of Contract: The period of contract shall be from date of award to July 31, 2028. There are three (3) option periods of one (1) year to be exercised at the discretion of the Department. Työt tehdään tilaajan laadituttamien suunnitelmien mukaan. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana. Tilaaja hankkii pääurakkaan alistettavina sivu-urakoina: putki-, ilmanvaihto-, sähkö- ja rakennusautomaatiourakat. Rakennusurakoitsija toimii myös urakan ajan kohteen päätoteuttajana sekä työmaan johtovelvollisuuksista ja työmaapalveluista vastaavana urakoitsijana. Vuonna 1966 valmistuneeseen koulurakennukseen tehdään sisäpuolinen peruskorjaus ja kohteen piha-alueelle tehdään muutoksia. Isoimpina muutoksia pintarakenteiden uusimisien lisäksi ovat mm. ruokasalin ja keittiön uusiminen toiseen sijaintiin rakennuksessa, kahden hissin rakentaminen, katolla olevien IV-konehuoneiden laajennukset koneineen sekä alapohjarakenteiden uusimiset suunnitelmien mukaan ja purunpoistotilan laajennus. title: Aviapoliksen lukion ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta
description: Aviapoliksen lukion ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta Vantaan kaupungin Aviapoliksen lukiolle tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Aviapoliksen lukio otetaan käyttöön asteittain. Alkuvaiheessa vuonna 2027 opiskelijoita arvioidaan olevan 90 opiskelijaa. Henkilökuntaa arvioidaan olevan alkuvaiheessa noin 2-15 henkilöä. Vuonna 2028 oppilasmäärän arvioidaan olevan noin 530 ja henkilökuntaa noin 15-20 henkilöä ja vuonna 2029 oppilasmäärä on arviolta 700 oppilasta. Vuoden 2029 tarkkaa henkilökuntamäärää ei vielä ole tiedossa. Tilaaja valitsee enintään yhden (1) sopimustoimittajan. Sopimus tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa olevaksi. Sopimuksen ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa sopimusluonnoksissa (liite 1 ja 2). Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa arvioituihin hankintamääriin tai euromääräisiin arvoihin sopimuskaudella. Tarjoajien tarjouksien määrittelemisen helpottamiseksi, Tilaaja järjestää kohteeseen yhteisnäyttöpäivän. Tarjoajien on osallistuttava yhteisnäyttöpäivään, ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Tarjouspyynnön kohteena olevat tilat ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden osalta esitellään seuraavasti: Aviapoliksen lukio, 26.10.2026 klo 9.00 Kohteen tilojen esittelytilaisuuksiin tulee ilmoittautua viimeistään 23.10.2026 klo 16.00 mennessä sähköpostitse osoitteeseen ostoyksikko.puhtauspalvelut@vantaa.fi. Tarjoajien tasapuolisen ja syrjimättömän kohtelun vuoksi tarjoajien kohteissa esittämiin kysymyksiin ei vastata. Kaikki yhteisnäyttökierroksilla esiin tulleet kysymykset tulee esittää tarjouspalvelu.fi:n kautta, jonka kautta annetaan myös vastaukset tulleisiin kysymyksiin. Tarjoajan tulee todistaa henkilöllisyys osallistuessaan yhteisnäyttöön. Lisätietoja yhteisnäyttöpäivästä löytyy kohdasta Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit.,

title: Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service
description: Reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service Gasgrid Finland Oy (hereinafter “Contracting Authority”) is a state-owned gas transmission system operator (TSO) that started operating in early 2020. The company mission is to ensure cost-effective, safe and undisturbed gas transmission and to actively develop the gas market and the Finnish energy system. The company has the overall system responsibility for the entire methane gas transmission network in Finland. The Contracting Authority is planning to construct a natural gas compression station to Lempäälä, Finland. Construction work is scheduled to be started approx. Q2/2027. Installation of the compressor unit(s) is planned to be started approx. Q2/2028. The schedule mentioned is indicative and subject to changes. In this procurement the Contracting Authority is looking for a supplier for 2+1 (option) complete, electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor packages for natural gas compression service to Gasgrid’s Lempäälä gas compression station. The key specifications as follows (but not limited to these): - Each compressor package shall comprise one electrically driven API 618 reciprocating compressor unit, together with the associated process equipment, auxiliaries, electrical equipment, instrumentation, control and safety systems, and other equipment necessary to provide a complete, safe and operable compressor package suitable for integration into the Compressor Station. - The Supplier shall be responsible for the design, manufacture, testing, documentation, delivery, integration and conformity of the complete compressor package within the final agreed scope of supply. The Supplier shall also be responsible for defining and managing the necessary technical and safety interfaces between the compressor package and systems or equipment supplied by the Contracting Authority, EPCM Contractor or other parties, to the extent necessary for the safe integration and conformity of the compressor package. - The anticipated operating envelope of each compressor unit is approximately 3,000 Nm³/h, with suction pressure approximately 4–8 barg and discharge pressure up to approximately 54 barg. -The compressor packages shall comply with all applicable European Union and Finnish legislation and requirements, including the applicable requirements of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex V, Part A – Declaration of Conformity for Completed Machinery, PED 2014/68/EU, ATEX 2014/34/EU and EMC 2014/30/EU. -The Supplier shall be capable of fulfilling the applicable manufacturer obligations and conformity assessment requirements for the complete compressor package, including provision of the required declarations, CE marking and conformity documentation. Site supervision and commissioning support, including support for the required on-site conformity and CE marking activities, are included. Installation at site is excluded from the scope of supply. Detailed technical requirements, operating conditions, performance requirements, scope boundaries, interfaces and documentation requirements will be defined in the procurement documentation issued during the subsequent phase of the procurement procedure.,

title: Anskaffelsesbistand til Forsvarsmateriell
description: Forsvarsmateriell (FMA) har tre hovedoppgaver: å anskaffe, forvalte og utfase materiell for Forsvaret og øvrige virksomheter i forsvarssektoren. Målet er å gi Forsvaret raskere reaksjonsevne, høyere beredskap og lengere utholdenhet. FMA Anskaffelser inngår, forvalter, gjør avrop på rammeavtaler og inngår kontrakter på/anskaffer materiell i henhold til lov og forskrift om offentlige anskaffelser (LOA/FOA/FOSA) samt interne instrukser. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å inngå avtale med leverandører som kan bistå oppdragsgiver med gjennomføringen av anskaffelser. Bistanden skal dekke alle deler av anskaffelsesprosessen, herunder planlegging utarbeidelse av konkurransegrunnlag, gjennomføring av konkurranse, evaluering av tilbud, samt kontraktsinngåelse og for enkelte kategorier; kontraktsoppfølging. title: 6515--Philips Lithium-Ion Batteries and Barcode Scanner
description: This RFI is solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. Per FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not considered offers, shall not be used as a proposal, and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Neither unsolicited proposals nor any other kinds of offers will be considered in response to this notice. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents; however, the Government does reserve the right to contact any respondent and/or respondent reference to obtain additional information. At this time, no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. Any resulting procurement action will be the subject of a separate, future announcement. The information is provided for discussion purposes and any potential strategy for this acquisition may change prior to any solicitation release. The acquisition strategy, evaluation methodology, contract type, and any other acquisition decisions are to be determined. STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Contract Title. Philips VS30 Batteries Background. Replacement: The DC VA Medical Center has a requirement to replace the existing Philips Medical VS30 Vital Signs batteries. The current VS30 vital signs batteries were purchased in 2025, have reached end of life, and are no longer usable. The VS30 battery life is 2 years and aligns with OEM preventative maintenance (PM) requirements. Only the VS30 vital signs monitors are being impacted, and the batteries must fully integrate with the existing Philips VS30 devices. Also requesting additional scanners for deployment and inventory. Scope of Work. The procurement shall include all parts, materials, labor, software/licenses, resources, and training required to implement and utilize the equipment/system to their fullest capacity. All items must be covered by manufacturer s warranty and procured through a manufacturer-approved distribution channel. Distributers and resellers must be able to document ability to provide items through manufacturer-approved distribution channels upon request. Specifications. 4.1 Equipment Line Item Description Quantity BATTERY PACK, 9-CELLS LITHIUM-ION, BLACK, 7.8AH CAPACITY, 11.1V VOLTAGE, FOR USE WITH: FOR VS30 EARLYVUE MONITOR by Philips / 989803199221 400 Periph HS-1 RFID Barcode Scanner (HS-1RS) / 989803225411 30 VSM roll stand barcode scanner holder / 989803210381 30 4.2 Required Features This battery must be the exact same as the BATTERY PACK, 9-CELLS LITHIUM-ION, BLACK, 7.8AH CAPACITY, 11.1V VOLTAGE, FOR USE WITH: FOR VS30 EARLYVUE MONITOR by Philips / 989803199221 to be compatible with the Philips VS30 Vital Signs monitor. Battery Capacity: 7.35 Ah Battery Chemistry: Lithium Ion Dimensions: 5.88 x 3.50 x 0.78 in Weight: 2.87 lbs Voltage: 11.1V The scanners must be the HS-1RS model to ensure compatibility and connectivity with active workflow and environment. Other scanners will require added costs, procedures, and networking which is not included in this package. Specific Tasks. 5.1 Delivery. All equipment shall be delivered to: Washington DC VA Medical Center 50 Irving St NW Washington, DC 20422 ATTN: VHAWAS Equipment Committee Contract VA Purchase Order (PO) number shall be included with delivery information (e.g., packing slip). Note: PO number starts with station code 688 followed by a letter and 5 digits (e.g., 688A12345) Delivery Hours: The Warehouse is open to receive deliveries Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., excluding holidays. Contractor shall coordinate delivery with the on-site Point of Contact (POC) and provide shipment tracking information. Contractor shall verify delivery date and time with the on-site POC at least 3 business days prior to scheduled delivery. Delivery is required within 90 days from award of the contract. 5.2 On Site Procedures. COVID-19 Screening: All persons entering the facility shall be subject to screening for COVID-19 per the current CDC (Center for Disease Control) guidelines. Mask Requirement: All contractors shall wear masks while indoors. Contract personnel are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government Officials. Time spent on site shall be for a period sufficient to complete the work set forth in the statement of work. On site visits shall be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC. Contractor shall check in and out with Biomedical Engineering prior to visiting the worksite for each day of work. The VA campus is non-smoking. Contractor personnel are required to comply with this policy. Parking: it is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate designated parking areas. Contractor personnel s tool bags are subject to inspection. 5.3 Installation/Implementation. Installation/Implementation will be completed by personnel certified and knowledgeable with the designated equipment/system. Installation shall be completed within the period of performance. Contractor shall be responsible for any Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required when performing work on site. Contractor shall submit all removable media to be used on a VA system to Biomedical Engineering for scanning with anti-virus software prior to use. In the case turn-in, exchange, repair, or replacement of equipment containing hard drives used by the VA, the hard drives shall be removed from the equipment and remain in possession of the VA (this includes loaned or rented equipment). The contractor shall take all necessary precautions to prevent damage to any government property. The contractor shall report any damages immediately and shall be assessed current replacement costs for property damaged by the contractor, unless corrective action is taken. Any damaged material (i.e., trees, shrubs, lawn/turf, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, etc.) will be replaced in a timely manner or corrected by the contractor with like materials, at no extra cost to the government, upon approval of the Contracting Officer. 5.4 Training. Contractor shall be responsible for providing training to clinical staff/users. Training is to be scheduled in advance with the designated on-site POC. Education shall be provided prior to and/or at time of installation. Education professional shall be certified to provide instruction on the designated equipment/system. Education curriculum must include: operations and set-up, user maintenance, safety, and user troubleshooting tips. 5.5 Inspection and Acceptance. Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site POC upon completion of installation. In the event deficiencies are identified, the contractor shall provide the date when the identified deficiencies will be addressed if not addressed on the date of installation. The Contractor shall conduct a joint inspection with the on-site POC after addressing all deficiencies. All deficiencies identified in the joint inspections shall be corrected by the Contractor prior to Government acceptance of the item. Any disputes shall be resolved by the Contracting Officer. 5.6 Deliverables. The Contractor shall provide the below documentation for the proposed equipment to VHAWASEquipmentRequests@va.gov within 10 business days of work completion: Service report. Warranty information. Electronic copy of the Operators Manual. Electronic copies of the complete technical service manuals, including troubleshooting guides, necessary diagnostic software and equipment information, schematic diagrams, and parts lists. Hours of Operation. DC VAMC s normal business hours are Monday-Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, excluding observed Federal holidays: New Year s Day Labor Day Martin Luther King s Birthday Columbus Day President s Day Veteran s Day Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day Juneteenth Christmas Day Independence Day Any other national holiday as declared by the President of the United States Period o

title: FCI Fairton 2nd Qtr Subsistence
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with (IAW) the format in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number is 15B20427Q00000001 and this solicitation is issued as a Request For Quote (RFQ). Solicitation is for Second Quarter Subsistence, FY 2027 (Kosher, Meat, Frozen, and Dry). For a list, description and total quantities of all items refer to attached Standard Form 1449, Section 2. Solicitation is a 100% small business set aside. Any quotes from large businesses will not be considered. The NAICS for this requirement is 311999. Terms of delivery are F.O.B. destination to: FCI Fairton, 655 Fairton-Millville Road, Fairton, New Jersey 08320. Items will be awarded individually. More than one item may be awarded to one contractor. Evaluation Factors are price and past performance. Vendors who submit a quote concurs that delivery dates will be met, unless otherwise noted. Vendors should not quote on items which cannot be delivered for any reason. The Government reserves the right upon award to make a formal single award or multiple awards based on best value. The Government will award to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer, conforming to the solicitation, is considered to be the most advantageous to the Government. Past performance: A record of poor performance due to failure to deliver items within the expected delivery time period, requests to remove an item from a signed purchase order on previous awards, requests to disregard or cancel a signed purchase order, or poor quality may result in a poor performance rating. FCI Fairton will award quoted items to vendors that have a high past performance record IAW FAR 13.106-2(4) (ii) regardless of the quotes with the lowest price. Quotes from vendors without poor past performance represent the best value when compared to any lower priced quote(s). DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS: � All deliveries must be palletized unless prior arrangements were agreed to by FCI Fairton warehouse staff and/or material handlers (no side-loaded pallets). � All non-frozen, perishable foods must be delivered between 36 degrees F and 41 degrees F. � All canned goods must be delivered above 36 degrees F and not frozen. � All frozen foods must be delivered at 0 degrees F or below. �Frozen product after being received is subject to further inspection upon thawing to verify sizes/weights are within the Purchase Order and/or BOP National Specifications.� � Some items may require thawing and cooking to determine specification compliance and product wholesomeness. � Any product that indicates prior thawing will be refused. � All certified religious diet items must be marked with Kosher Symbol on individual packages or the item will be refused. � Items which are conditionally received and found noncompliant, must be picked up at the vendors� expense within (2) weeks of noncompliance notification. � Items that fail to meet specifications will be refused. All items must be dated. � Hours for delivery are 6:30 AM � 1:00PM, Mon-Fri, first come first serve. No deliveries on weekends or federal holidays. � Unless otherwise stated within the specification of an item description in Section 2 of SF Form 1449, all dates for frozen food items must be delivered frozen and delivered before the best buy date, sell by date, use by date, best if used by date, or freeze by date on the label. Substitutions to specifications in line items are prohibited (ex., case counts). Changes to specifications will not be evaluated and therefore, not considered for award. The government reserves the right upon inspection to reject items if they are damaged or not to the specifications as listed in the solicitation. Do not change the case counts or the quote of the item will not be considered. The date and time for receipt of offers is November 19, 2026 at 9:00 AM EST. Quote must indicate Solicitation No. 15B20427Q00000001 time specified for receipt of quote, name, address and telephone number of quote, technical description of the items being quoted in sufficient detail to evaluate compliance with the requirements in the solicitation, terms of any expressed warranty, price and any discount terms. Quote must include acknowledgment of amendments, if any. Expected award date is on or before December 18, 2026. A Notice of Award will be created and posted on sam.gov. Purchases in the amount of $15,000.01 and above will be made via purchase orders with payment by electronic funds transfer. Purchases in the amount of $15,000.00 and below will be made via a Government purchase card. Quotes will be FOB DESTINATION with expected delivery from January 4, 2027 through January 30, 2027. Any items shipped before or after the expected delivery dates will be returned at vendor�s expense.

title: Stage 2 - Sulphur Mountain Boardwalk Repairs, Banff National Park
description: Parks Canada Agency requires the services of a qualified Contractor to complete repair work on an existing boardwalk structure located on Sulphur Mountain in Banff National Park. The boardwalk is situated in a remote environment with significant access and logistical constraints. The scope of work includes but is not limited to, structural steel member replacements and welded repairs. Access to the site is restricted to helicopter access for materials and equipment delivery and gondola access for workers. There is limited on-site staging or laydown areas, and an off-site staging area will be required for material, equipment and helicopter long line staging. Construction activities, materials, and equipment must be transported to and from the site using helicopter-supported access, requiring careful planning and coordination to safely and efficiently execute the work within a sensitive national park environment. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

France – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Caractérisation géotechnique du ballast
description: Dans le cadre des opérations de renouvellement de la voie ferrée, SNCF Réseau souhaite caractériser le complexe ballasté dégarni. En effet, des prélèvements en voie du ballast en vue d’une analyse de la forme géotechnique (forme du grain, dureté) sont nécessaires dans le cadre des études préliminaires des chantiers à venir. Cette prestation s’inscrit dans le projet stratégique SNCF Réseau, de valorisation des sous-produits ferroviaires et de développement du réemploi du ballast. En particulier, le cahier des charges décrit les prestations à réaliser afin d’effectuer des prélèvements des échantillons de ballast en voie et des analyses géotechniques en laboratoire, en vue de définir les conditions de réutilisation/réemploi avant réalisation de travaux. L’objectif est d’obtenir les informations suivantes sur le ballast en voie, à renouveler : -L’état de vieillissement -Les performances intrinsèques -La qualité globale La prestation à assurer est divisé en quatre missions. Ces prestations peuvent être de différentes natures et commandées indépendamment les unes aux autres : - Mission 1 : Définition du programme de prélèvement en fonction des informations transmises par le demandeur (et élaboration du devis). - Mission 2 : Réalisation des prélèvements et remise en état - Mission 3 : Conditionnement des échantillons et réalisation des analyses en laboratoire - Mission 4 : Livrables Les sites à étudier sont en exploitation ferroviaire. Le marché est alloti en 4 lots géographiques, et se présente sous forme d'un accord-cadre à bons de commande (multi-attributaires pour chaque lot). Chaque lot est conclu pour une durée ferme de 24 mois.

description: Laundry Room Sink Installation This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Kent Institution, Pacific Region. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is open to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous businesses. All interested suppliers may participate. However, suppliers are to note that this requirement is subject to a preference for Indigenous suppliers and will be set-aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) if Canada receives two or more responsive bids from Indigenous businesses who meet the requirements of the PSIB. Indigenous businesses that have not already registered in the Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory should do so. Additional information on the Indigenous Business Directory is available at the following link: https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100033057/1610797769658#c3. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada requires a qualified contractor to install and commission sixteen (16) laundry sinks at Kent Institution in Agassiz, British Columbia. Objectives: To provide sixteen (16) secure, durable inmate-use sinks within the laundry rooms of the Courtyard Living Units to reduce unnecessary inmate movement between housing areas and centralized dishwashing locations and improve institutional operations, security, and staff efficiency through enhanced functionality of existing living unit spaces. Deliverables: The Contractor must: • Supply and install sixteen (16) laundry room sink stations. • Complete plumbing connections to existing domestic water and sanitary drainage systems. • Provide test and commission documentation confirming satisfactory operation of all installed plumbing systems. • Include product data sheets and warranty documentation for all major installed equipment and fixtures. • Include as-built drawings identifying any significant deviations. • Complete deficiency correction and closeout documentation as requested by CSC. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Construction Time: The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within fifteen (15) weeks from the date of notification of acceptance of the offer. File Number: 21807-27-5524015 Contracting Authority: Carlie Skotynski Telephone number: 604-756-4761 Facsimile number: 604-756-4761 E-mail: Carlie.Skotynski@csc-scc.gc.ca NOTE TO BIDDERS: Bidders can obtain the complete statement of work and evaluation criteria by downloading the solicitation document and associated documents from the Canada buys / tender opportunities website. The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French). After contract award, bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. description: De doelstelling van deze Europese openbare aanbesteding is het selecteren en contracteren van één Inschrijver voor het correctieve en preventieve onderhoud van de openbare verlichting in de gemeente Borne. De openbare verlichting in gemeente Borne omvat in hoofdzaak 5666 lichtmasten met één of meerdere armaturen. De masten zijn voor het merendeel aluminium masten. Ca. 5700 verlichtingsobjecten zijn aangesloten op Enexis Netbeheer- met uitzondering van het sportpark. Informatie van de schakel- en verdeelkasten en ondergrondse bekabeling is beschikbaar. Het aantal armaturen bedraagt ca. 5700, waarvan 99% LED.

title: Netherlands – Construction work – Raamovereenkomst Duurzaamheid en EML-maatregelen
description: De opdracht betreft het integraal voorbereiden en realiseren van energiebesparende maatregelen (EML) binnen de vastgoedportefeuille van Defensie, met als doel om de gebouwen tijdig te laten voldoen aan de wettelijke energiebesparingsplicht en bij te dragen aan de verduurzaming van het Rijksvastgoed. title: FCC Terre Haute condensation pumps and motor assemblies
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Complex (FCC) Terre Haute, Indiana, is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation for the requirements of 15B41827Q00000002 for condensation pumps and motor assemblies. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. This solicitation is unrestricted. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 333415. All quotes should include shipping costs, FOB destination. All products must meet the specifications of the pump and motor assemblies contained within the Statement of Work. Equivalent products may be submitted with full technical documentation for Government evaluation. It is known that the pump and motor assembly that are in place may be obsolete. It is the contractors� responsibility to best match a new assembly to meet the current specifications. All known information about the products requested can be found in the statement of work and the request for quote documents. The Government will award to the responsible offeror whose quote, conforming to the solicitation, are considered to be best value to the Government, with Price, Past Performance and Delivery time considered. Deliveries will be made to FCC Terre Haute. Located at 4700 Bureau Road South, Terre Haute, Indiana 47802 (812) 238- 1531. We will accept quotations with delivery dates past the targeted delivery date of January 28, 2026, and quotations with partial deliveries. Lead times and deliveries will be part of our evaluation process as we would prefer a single award for all items delivered on or before the targeted date. The following MUST be completed before your offer can be accepted: Representations and Certifications: Please ensure that your registration is active and up to date in the online System for Award Management. The link is www.sam.gov. Submission of your offer constitutes compliance. Standard Form (SF) 1449 - Solicitation/Contract/Order for Commercial Items. Please complete blocks 17a, 20, 30a, 30b, and 30c of the SF 1449 and the attached quote sheets (Please include offeror name & UEI number in header section of quote sheets). Please include your email address and UEI number in block 20. Original signatures are required on quotes submitted. The quote will be evaluated per FAR 12.203 and the government may then issue a purchase order (contract) that must be signed by both parties to complete contractual agreement. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 4.203-1(b) requires all contractors seeking or currently doing business with the government to be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award; information can be obtained at https://www.sam.gov/. All future information about this solicitation, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this solicitation. Please complete the attached Request for Quote, (RFQ) SF-1449 for submission of offers. The date for receipt of quotes is November 19th, 2026, by 11:00 AM EST. Payment will be made using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) through a purchase order. Completed AND signed quotes must be sent electronically to C1livingston@bop.gov. Faxed bids or hand carried quotes will NOT be accepted. Thank you for your interest and if you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me by email at C1livingston@bop.gov or 812-244-4400, ext. 4476. All question inquiries must be submitted by November 12th, 2026, by 11:00 AM EST. AI (artificial intelligence)/ SI (Super Intelligence) Disclaimer- The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or similar software tools, Super Intelligence (SI) to assist in the preparation of quotations is permitted; however, quoters are responsible for thoroughly reviewing and validating all generated content prior to submission. AI-generated text may contain repetitive language, generic phrasing, inaccuracies, or references to outdated policies, regulations, and procurement requirements. It is the vendor's responsibility to ensure that all quotation content is accurate, relevant, and compliant with current federal acquisition regulations and solicitation requirements. Vendors should be aware that the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) has adopted applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part deviations associated with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). Quotations should reflect compliance with all current FAR requirements, deviations, and related guidance in effect at the time of submission. Sincerely, Carl Livingston Contract Specialist

title: J065--Notice of Intenet to Sole Source- Life Technologies Corporation Maintenance and Service for QuantStudio 12K Flex Real-Time Quantitation System
description: SPECIAL NOTICE NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE I. The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77056 in support of Central Arkansas Veterans Heath Care System (CAVHS), intends to solicit and award Sole Source, Firm-Fixed-Price, contract with a base year and four one-year ordering periods to one large business (LB) source, Life Technologies Corporation. Life Technologies Corporation. 5781 Van Allen Way Carlsbad, CA 92008 The Central Arkansas Veterans Heath care System (CAVHS) has a requirement for maintenance and repair of the following equipment: QuantStudio 12K Flex Real-Time Quantitation System Serial Number: 285881052 Associated system controller/computer, as identified in the resulting contract The equipment is located at the John L. McClellan Veterans Hospital in Little Rock, Arkansas. Required Services: The contractor shall furnish all personnel, supervision, labor, travel, transportation, tools, test equipment, replacement parts, software support, technical data, and other resources necessary to maintain the covered equipment in accordance with manufacturer operating and safety specifications. 1. Corrective maintenance and repair; 2. At least one scheduled preventive-maintenance inspection during each contract period; 3. Labor, travel, and replacement parts required for covered repairs; 4. Telephone and email technical support; 5. Remote diagnostic support through a VA-approved connection and in accordance with applicable VA information-security requirements; 6. Manufacturer-approved software, firmware, quality, safety, and field-service updates; 7. Access to proprietary diagnostic tools and technical information necessary to perform maintenance; 8. Service by qualified technicians trained to maintain the QuantStudio 12K Flex system; 9. Written service reports identifying work performed, parts installed, test equipment used, and test-equipment calibration status; and 10. Restoration of the equipment to manufacturer operating specifications following maintenance or repair. Only new original-equipment-manufacturer parts, or parts expressly approved by the manufacturer for the covered system, shall be installed. The contract price for each period shall include all covered labor, parts, travel, preventive maintenance, remote support, and technical support. Work outside the contract scope may not begin unless separately authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer through an executed contract modification. Service Levels Telephone or email acknowledgment: Within one business hours after receipt of a service request during established coverage hours. Remote diagnostics: Initiated promptly following acknowledgment of the service request. Onsite response: A qualified technician shall arrive within 4 business hours after determining that the problem cannot be resolved remotely. Service hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time, excluding federal holidays. The anticipated contract will include a base year and four one-year ordering periods. Exercise of each ordering period will be at the sole discretion of the Government and subject to the availability of funds. II. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 811210 - Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance. Size Standard $34.0. III. This procurement is being conducted under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 12.102 (a) Restricting Competition and FAR 5.001- Notice of Proposed Contract Action. This notice is not a request for quotes, but rather a notice of intent to sole source. IV. The anticipated award date is April 18, 2027. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract. Anticipated Periods of Performance Contract Period Anticipated Dates Base Year April 18, 2027 - April 17, 2028 Option Year 1 April 18, 2028 - April 17, 2029 Option Year 2 April 18, 2029 - April 17, 2030 Option Year 3 April 18, 2030 - April 17, 2031 Option Year 4 April 18, 2031 - April 17, 2032 V. Please note that this is not a request for competitive quotes and is being posted for informational purposes only. The government does not anticipate receiving responses to this notice. However, interested parties who disagree with this action may submit a letter of interest that demonstrates your firm s technical expertise, original equipment manufacturer (OEM) authorization letter and personnel OEM training/ certifications to perform services. In addition, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the complete requirement may submit a written capability statement containing: Legal business name, physical address, Unique Entity ID, and point of contact; Business size and applicable socioeconomic status under NAICS 811210. Evidence of active registration in the System for Award Management. Evidence of authorization to service the QuantStudio 12K Flex system. Evidence that proposed technicians possess appropriate manufacturer training. Evidence of access to proprietary diagnostic tools, service software, technical documentation, updates, service bulletins, and manufacturer-approved replacement parts. Relevant experience maintaining or repairing QuantStudio 12K Flex systems. Commercially available telephone, remote, and onsite response times. Ability to begin full performance by April 18, 2027. Ability to provide continuous coverage for the base period and, if exercised, each of the four ordering periods. Identification of proposed subcontractors and the work each subcontractor would perform. A general statement of capability, reseller status, or experience with unrelated laboratory equipment will not, by itself, demonstrate the ability to satisfy the requirement. The government reserves the right to verify any request for additional documentation submitted. VI. Interested parties shall identify their interests, provide OEM authorization, personnel certifications /training as mentioned in section V of this document and capability to meet the government requirements and respond to this notice within fifteen (15) calendar days of the publication of this notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Interested parties may identify their interest solely via email to Contracting Officer, Anthony Marion, Anthony.marion2@va.gov no later than November 19, 2026 10:00am Central Standard Time (CST). When responding to this announcement, respondents should include 36C25627Q0118 Notice of Intent" in the subject line. Questions shall be submitted no later than November 9, 2026, 10:00am Central Standard Time (CST). VII. Late responses may not be accepted. No telephone inquiries will be accepted nor will phone calls be returned. Only emailed responses will be considered. Information received will be utilized solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination not to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is at the sole discretion of the Government.

Germany – Landscaping work for green areas – U4-Verlängerung auf die Horner Geest - Ersatzpflanzungen, Landschaftsbauarbeiten, Grünflächen und Stellplatzflächen im Abschnitt 2 [ba]
description: Die Hamburger Hochbahn baut derzeit die Verlängerung der U-Bahn-Linie U4 nach Osten, um auch den Stadtteil Horn an das U-Bahn-Netz anzuschließen. In einem ersten Bauabschnitt wurde bereits u. a. die Haltestelle Horner Rennbahn erweitert und fertiggestellt. Die Baumersatzpflanzungen und Landschaftsbauarbeiten wurden hier bereits durchgeführt. Im zweiten Bauabschnitt entsteht die neue U4-Strecke mit den Haltestellen Stoltenstraße und Horner Geest, die im Dezember 2027 in Betrieb gehen soll.. Der zweite Bauabschnitt beginnt östlich der Straße Hermannstal und folgt der Manshardtstraße nach Osten bis zur Straße Silberberg. Der U-Bahn-Tunnel wurde in offener Bauweise erstellt und verläuft zum Großteil unter der Manshardtstraße, die zurzeit wiederhergestellt wird. Die Länge dieses Abschnitts der Manshardtstraße beträgt rd. 1,6 km. Zu beiden Seiten der Manshardtstraße müssen Flächen entlang der gesamten Länge wiederhergestellt werden. Für Bewegungs- und Baustelleneinrichtungsflächen wurden seitlich der Baugrube Privatflächen, öffentliche Grünflächen und Schulhofflächen abgeräumt und in Anspruch genommen. Diese Flächen müssen ebenso wiederhergestellt werden. Die größeren wiederherzustellenden Baustelleneinrichtungs-Flächen (Bodenlager, Betonwerk und Wasseraufbereitungsanlage) befinden sich auf der Horner Rennbahn.

title: BATDOK Family of Systems (FoS)
description: Please review the full RFI document (Atch 1) for full details and instructions. A. Notice to Respondents This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e). It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Commercial Solutions Opening, and it is not a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted or for any cost incurred in responding. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not provide feedback or evaluations to individual respondents. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking proprietary information. The Government will protect properly marked information from disclosure and may share responses with Government support contractors bound by non-disclosure agreements. Do not submit classified information. B. Purpose The Defense Health Agency (DHA), Program Acquisition Executive, Medical Digital Solutions (PAE MDS), Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems (JOMIS) Program Management Office (PMO), is issuing this RFI to conduct market research for the operations and sustainment (O&S) of the Battlefield Assisted Trauma Distributed Observation Kit (BATDOK) family of systems (FoS). The anticipated period of performance begins 1 October 2027 (Fiscal Year 2028). The BATDOK FoS is comprised of BATDOK-J, an Android and iOS mobile application for point-of-injury (PoI) casualty documentation; BATDOK Link, a Windows operating system application plug-in that allows for the transfer of data from BATDOK-J into MHS GENESIS Theater (MHSG-T) or Operational Medicine Data Service (OMDS) via QR code; and BAT-TAK, a plug-in for the Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK). The FoS is a mature capability, fielded and in operational use across the Military Services. The purpose of this RFI is to: Identify potential sources, including small businesses, with demonstrated DoW experience developing, sustaining, and integrating tactical mobile applications on the Android and iOS operating systems, together with associated ATAK and Windows plug-ins; Obtain industry input on technical approaches, best practices, and innovations for achieving the outcomes described in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) in Part II; and Inform the Government�s acquisition strategy, including contract vehicle, contract type, small business set-aside determination, and refinement of the requirement and its performance measures.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE MODIFICATION Security Guard Services � CDC Facilities, Metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado Contract No. 75D30125C20468 NAICS Code: 561612, Security Guards and Patrol Services (size standard: $29 Million Dollars) Place of Performance: CDC-owned and leased facilities, metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado Period of the Proposed Action: January 1, 2027 through January 31, 2027 Response Date: 1:00 PM Eastern Time, November 19, 2026 Intent and Authority The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) intends to negotiate a sole-source modification to Contract No. 75D30125C20468 with Chenega Global Protection, LLC for one month of continued security guard services covering January 1 through January 31, 2027. The proposed action is authorized under FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements (41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1)). Purpose The modification will maintain continuous, uninterrupted security guard coverage at CDC facilities in metro Atlanta, Georgia and Fort Collins, Colorado during the January 2027 transition-in period of the competitively awarded follow-on contract. The ongoing requirement for these services has been competed; this action is confined to the single transition month. Basis for the Sole-Source Determination Chenega Global Protection, LLC is the only responsible source able to perform this requirement without interruption during the January 1�31, 2027 window. The requirement is not merely to perform security guard services for one month. It is to assume full coverage of the security of multiple CDC campuses, including a BSL-4 select-agent laboratory and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) posts on January 1, 2027 with no lapse, and to relinquish those posts to the follow-on contractor on February 1, 2027. Guard personnel at these posts must already hold the requisite security clearances, CDC facility credentials and access badges, site- and post-specific certifications, and current weapons qualifications. The incumbent�s workforce is already fully cleared, credentialed, badged, post-certified, and in place. Any source other than the incumbent would first have to complete its own transition-in � clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification � before January 1, 2027, and then immediately execute a transition-out thirty days later. The Government has determined, and has structured the follow-on contract to reflect, that a new contractor requires the full period of January 1�31, 2027 to complete transition-in alone. Any lapse, gap, or partial coverage would create an unacceptable risk to life safety, to the physical security of select agents at the BSL-4 laboratory, and to classified national-security information within the SCIF. Accordingly, for this limited period, only one responsible source can satisfy the agency�s requirement. Capability Statements All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which the agency will consider. To be responsive, a capability statement should address how the respondent would complete transition-in at the identified CDC facilities � including security clearances, credentialing, badging, post certification, and weapons qualification � so as to assume full post coverage effective January 1, 2027, and complete transition-out to the follow-on contractor by January 31, 2027, with no lapse or degradation in coverage at any point during the period. Notice Limitations This notice is not a request for competitive quotations and is not a solicitation. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice. Submission Instructions Capability statements must be received by Contracting Officer Mike Davis at VWL8@CDC.GOV no later than 1:00 PM Eastern Time on November 19, 2026. Responses received after that time will not be considered.

description: This is a Special Notice of the Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board's (FRTIB) intent to award a sole source contract to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA), 300 Seventh Street, SW, Washington, DC 20024, for transit subsidy administration services. The contemplated award will provide access to WMATA's SmartBenefits� Program, which enables the electronic distribution and administration of transit benefits for eligible FRTIB employees participating in the Federal Transit Benefit Program. The anticipated period of performance is one (1) twelve-month base period and nineteen (19) twelve-month option periods. Exercise of any option period is at the sole discretion of the Government. Authority The Government intends to award this requirement on a sole source basis pursuant to FAR 13.106-1(b), Soliciting from a Single Source, as only one source is reasonably available to satisfy the agency's requirements. Sole Source Rationale WMATA is the sole owner, operator, and administrator of the SmartBenefits� Program, the transit benefit system utilized throughout the National Capital Region. The SmartBenefits� Program provides the infrastructure required to electronically distribute transit subsidies directly to employee transit accounts for use with participating regional transit providers. FRTIB has determined that WMATA is the only source capable of fulfilling this requirement because: WMATA exclusively administers the SmartBenefits� Program. The SmartBenefits� Program is the established regional transit benefit platform accepted by participating transit providers throughout the Washington metropolitan area. No other vendor possesses the rights, authority, or capability to provide access to, administer, or distribute benefits through the SmartBenefits� Program. The use of an alternate source would not satisfy the Government's requirement for participation in the regional transit subsidy program. Capability Statements This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, any responsible source that believes it can satisfy the requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating its ability to provide the required services. Capability statements shall include sufficient information to clearly demonstrate the ability to provide transit subsidy administration services equivalent to those provided through WMATA's SmartBenefits� Program. Responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer by 1:30 pm, Thursday, November 19, 2026. The Government will consider all capability statements received by the closing date solely for the purpose of determining whether competitive sources exist. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Instructions for Responses: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions). The anticipated period of performance is a 5-year ordering period. After review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). Responses to this notice must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (Attachment A). All interested parties can provide written opinions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Responses to this notice shall be submitted via e-mail to Amanda Edger, Contract Specialist, at Amanda.Edger@fda.hhs.gov (with a CC: to Ian Weiss, Contracting Officer, at Ian.Weiss@fda.hhs.gov), by November 19, 2026, at 2:00 pm. After a review of the received responses, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.
